passages.title: A Wrong Turn on the Mountain Road
passages.text:
Last summer, Hung borrowed his uncle's car for a weekend trip. On the main road out of the city, a large sign showed the **speed limit**: sixty kilometres an hour. Hung stayed below it, even when a line of impatient drivers formed behind him. Later, the road began to climb into the hills, and a new sign appeared: **no overtaking**. This was important, because the bends were sharp and he could not see far ahead.

A young driver in a small red car ignored the sign. He tried to **overtake** Hung on a bend, just as a bus came round the corner from the opposite direction. Luckily, both cars stopped in time, but everyone was shaken. Hung, whose phone battery had died, then followed the wrong road and **ended up** in a tiny village he had never heard of. An old man at a café drew him a map on a paper napkin. "Better to arrive late than not to arrive at all," he said. Hung agreed and drove home slowly.
passages.summary_vi: Hùng lái xe của chú đi chơi cuối tuần, gặp biển giới hạn tốc độ và cấm vượt, suýt tai nạn vì một tài xế trẻ vượt xe, rồi lạc vào một ngôi làng lạ và được một cụ già vẽ đường về.

exercises.instruction: Match each word or phrase with its meaning.

exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with a word or phrase from the box.

items.explain: Sau 'might' dùng nguyên mẫu: might end up in (rốt cuộc lại ở).

passages.title: Learning to Cook
passages.text:
Mai had never been **a good cook**, and her friends often joked about it. When she moved into her own flat, she decided to change that. Her first rule was simple: **follow a recipe** carefully and never guess the measurements. Her second rule was to check that she **had all the ingredients** before she started, because last month she discovered halfway through making soup that there was no salt in the house.

On Sunday she made a three-part meal from a cookbook her grandmother gave her. First she had to **boil** the potatoes in a saucepan for fifteen minutes. Then she **roasted** a chicken in the oven until the skin turned golden. For dessert she **baked** an apple cake, which smelled wonderful when it came out. Roasting and baking both use the oven, but roasting is for meat or vegetables with oil, while baking is for cakes and bread. Her friends tasted everything and admitted that it was delicious. Mai smiled: she was finally getting better.
passages.summary_vi: Mai vốn không nấu ăn giỏi nên tự đặt quy tắc: làm đúng công thức và kiểm tra đủ nguyên liệu. Chủ nhật, cô luộc khoai, quay gà và nướng bánh táo, và bạn bè khen ngon.

passages.title: A Childhood in the Countryside
passages.text:
My cousin Lan **grew up in the countryside**, in a small village far from any big city. She often tells me that her childhood was the happiest time of her life. Her house stood **on the banks of the river**, and every morning she woke to the sound of running water. Behind the house there were **woods** where she and her friends played hide-and-seek and picked wild berries in summer.

What she remembers most is how clearly she could see **the seasons** change. In spring the fields turned bright green, in autumn the leaves became red and gold, and in winter mist covered the water. The **scenery** was so beautiful that tourists sometimes stopped to take photographs. Lan says that the **open spaces** taught her to feel free and calm. Now she lives in a crowded city, and she misses the quiet. "I did not know how lucky I was," she says, "until I had to live without it." Every holiday she returns to her old village to walk beside the river again.
passages.summary_vi: Lan lớn lên ở nông thôn, nhà bên bờ sông, gần khu rừng nhỏ, nhớ rõ bốn mùa và phong cảnh đẹp; giờ sống ở thành phố đông đúc, cô nhớ sự yên tĩnh và về thăm làng mỗi dịp nghỉ.

passages.title: A Health Campaign at Work
passages.text:
The health department of a large city wanted to **develop an effective strategy** to inform people about **hepatitis**, a serious liver disease that many people do not recognise. The team knew that ordinary posters would not be enough, so they decided to study how **consumers** get their health information. The research showed that most people trust short videos from doctors more than long leaflets.

Not everyone agreed on the best plan. During one meeting, a heated **argument** broke out between the designers, who wanted bright colours, and the doctors, who wanted detailed facts. The manager reminded everyone that they shared the same goal. After a difficult week, the team managed to **get through** the disagreement and agreed on a compromise: simple pictures with one clear message.

On the day of the launch the office lift broke down, so everyone had to **take the stairs** to the tenth floor, laughing and out of breath. The campaign was a success, and thousands of people booked a free health check.
passages.summary_vi: Một cơ quan y tế xây dựng chiến lược truyền thông về bệnh viêm gan, nghiên cứu cách người tiêu dùng tiếp nhận thông tin, vượt qua tranh cãi giữa nhà thiết kế và bác sĩ, và chiến dịch thành công.

items.explain: Argument là cuộc tranh cãi khi mọi người bất đồng ý kiến.

items.definition: to manage to deal with a difficult period or to finish something hard
items.explain: Get through là vượt qua một giai đoạn khó khăn hoặc hoàn thành việc khó.

items.definition: to go up or down a building using the steps instead of a lift

items.q: Doctors warned that ____ can damage the liver if it is not treated.
items.explain: Bệnh gây hại cho gan là hepatitis (viêm gan).

items.q: The company asked its students to ____ to attract more young customers.
items.explain: Xây dựng một chiến lược hiệu quả: develop an effective strategy. Sau 'to' dùng nguyên mẫu.

items.q: Online shops collect information about what ____ buy and when.
items.explain: Người mua hàng là consumers (số nhiều vì động từ 'buy' không có -s).

items.q: My sister and I had a loud ____ about whose turn it was to wash the dishes.
items.explain: Tranh cãi to tiếng là an argument; 'a loud ____' cần danh từ.

items.q: It was hard, but she managed to ____ her final exams with good marks.
items.explain: Sau 'managed to' dùng nguyên mẫu: get through (vượt qua kỳ thi).

items.q: The lift was out of order, so we had to ____ up to the fifth floor.
items.explain: Thang máy hỏng nên phải đi thang bộ: take the stairs.

items.q: What did the research show about health information?

Posters are always the best choice.
items.explain: Bài viết: 'most people trust short videos from doctors more than long leaflets'.

items.q: What caused the argument in the meeting?
options: Designers wanted bright colours while doctors wanted detailed facts.
items.explain: Nhà thiết kế muốn màu sắc nổi bật, còn bác sĩ muốn nhiều thông tin chi tiết.

items.q: Why did everyone take the stairs on the day of the launch?
items.explain: Bài viết: 'the office lift broke down'.
